unlisted_practices: Train AI models on population-representative, large and deep datasets built by multidisciplinary and multinational teams to avoid developer, statistical, and social bias.
Establish trust in a precompetitive space for collaborative, multi-institution and multinational health data use and AI development.
Support legislation and enforcement that prioritize regulating health data use, not only data protection, with effective legal deterrents against criminal decryption and reidentification.

Harmonize technical and administrative standards and contractual and consent documents (for example, transatlantic patient consent forms and an international patient summary) to enable interoperable collaborative data use.
Standardize opt-out and consent mechanisms for collaborative health data use, free of prejudice.
Ensure digital inclusion by engaging all stakeholders and reducing barriers for people with disabilities and the elderly.
Overcome the knowledge asymmetry around AI through education and training.
Build trust through model projects with explicit citizen and patient participation that demonstrate tangible benefits of collaborative data use and AI.
Adapt regulatory workflows for AI and require transparency (explainability), decision autonomy level, decision effect size, and opportunity for human oversight and override for regulatory approval.
Establish post-marketing surveillance and clarify developer and user liability for AI models that change over their lifecycle.
Use federated or swarm learning where appropriate to let institutions collaborate on model development without moving the physical location of data.
Do not use service robots in healthcare primarily to address manpower shortages or achieve cost control.
Jointly assess AI readiness with patients through continuous dialogue with citizens and patients.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/vision paper calling for transatlantic collaboration, governance, and health data sharing frameworks (e.g., European Health Data Space, G7 Hiroshima AI process) to support AI development and health data use.
